judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{success, data, error}`), but this call site assigns the whole wrapper to `key` and persists it — the pre-diff code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`'s parsed data directly. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` in the database becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of the credential object; every subsequent read of `credential.key.access_token`/`.refresh_token` yields undefined, so Google Calendar API calls fail auth for that user until manual re-install — in both sharing and non-sharing modes.

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, error }`) rather than the parsed credential data. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff changes `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials);` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That will store the wrapper object into `credential.key`, changing its shape and breaking later code that expects `credential.key.access_token` etc. This is verifiable directly from the new helper implementation and its call site.
